title: rag.py eval counts the good rows whose pack gains a check: note, so a note that misfires on answered questions fails the eval and not only the review
goal: rag.py eval prints the number of rows expected good whose pack carries a check: note or a route: line and fails when it rises above a recorded baseline, so a change to the pack's notes is caught by the item's eval check (SP-kp3boz7z: BG-xbbimxpq's eval check passed 621 of 621 while its passing note put a check: on three eval goods, found only by the review, BG-pedsqeqs)

run: import re,subprocess,sys;o=subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/rag.py","eval"],capture_output=True,text=True);m=re.search(r"noted=([0-9]+)",o.stdout);print(o.returncode,m and m.group(0));sys.exit(0 if o.returncode==0 and m else 1)

notes:
Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 1 of 19, "Lookup correctness: pack notes fire only where they should, and the eval counts a good row that gains one"): it serves the fitness tests of EP-gzr4mmkm: a lookup's verdict or the benchmark's measurement is wrong until it is fixed.
Premise: on 2026-10-12 (origin/main a5a7459f2) the summary line of rag.py eval (questions=630 passed=630 ...) has no count of noted goods and the eval exits 0 while three eval goods carry the passing note (BG-pedsqeqs).
The suite is at its id ceiling (100 of 100), so the old check named a test that cannot be added: extend pack_scatter_check, add no test id. Interface the checks read: run_eval's dict gains an integer noted, the summary line prints noted=N, and the module constant rag.NOTED_BASELINE bounds it: a count above it exits 1. The baseline is the count the eval prints once BG-pedsqeqs and BG-j7pe3u46 have landed (this item depends on both). tools.md says rag.py eval is unaffected by the notes: reword it. Check 1 passes before the work (the test it extends). AGENTS.md, content-rules.md and token-efficiency.md are in touches only as mapped docs: edit one only if stale (AGENTS.md is at its size cap).
